introduction: I use organic molecules to investigate past climate and environmental change. My work combines lipid biomarkers and compound-specific δ²H and δ¹³C measurements with other evidence preserved in lake sediments.
context: A central challenge is separating climatic signals from changes in the plants and aquatic organisms that produce the molecules we measure. I investigate these source effects through modern calibration studies and sedimentary records.

projects.title: MEMELAND
projects.summary: Reconstructing medieval land use from lake sediments, using fecal and plant biomarkers to trace farming practices and environmental impacts.
projects.question: How can molecular traces in lake sediments reveal medieval farming practices and their environmental impacts?
projects.about:
MEMELAND investigates how human land use has shaped European landscapes and biodiversity over the last two millennia. It combines lake-sediment archives with archaeological, palaeoecological, and molecular evidence to distinguish local land-use histories from regional change.

Read more about [the Eawag team’s research](https://memeland.no/en/Team/eawag.html).
projects.approach:
- **Grazing and manuring:** Fecal sterols and bile acids will trace animal and human inputs, complement animal sedimentary DNA records, and test links between nutrient enrichment and low-oxygen lake conditions.
- **Soil erosion:** Compound-specific radiocarbon dating of leaf waxes and refractory organic carbon analyses will investigate soil disturbance linked to ploughing and livestock.
- **Crop cultivation:** Miliacin (millet) and cannabinol (*Cannabis* spp.) will be used to investigate cultivation and practices such as hemp retting.

Biomarker records will be integrated with hyperspectral imaging and geochemical and chronological data from the University of Salzburg team. Together with archaeobotany, sedimentary DNA, and socio-environmental modelling, these records will help compare medieval agricultural practices across Europe.
projects.contribution: I will join Prof. [Nathalie Dubois](https://memeland.no/en/Team/people.html#prof.-dr.-nathalie-dubois) in the Eawag team’s biomarker work, using lake sediments to reconstruct medieval agricultural practices and their effects on aquatic ecosystems.

projects.title: ADAPT
projects.summary: Using lipid biomarkers and sedimentary DNA to understand how lake algal communities respond to natural change and human activity.
projects.question: How have natural change and human activity shaped lake algal communities over time?
projects.about:
ADAPT is a Swiss National Science Foundation project investigating the history of lake algae, whose communities affect water quality, food webs, and the carbon cycle. Lipid biomarkers and sedimentary DNA preserved in sediments provide complementary evidence of past algal occurrence and composition.

Our lake studies span Switzerland and the USA.
projects.approach:
- **Modern calibration:** Compare lipid biomarkers and sedimentary DNA in water and surface sediments with living algal communities.
- **Past algal dynamics:** Use Swiss lake sediments to investigate 20th-century phosphorus changes, Roman-period effects on water quality, and natural algal variability over the last 10,000 years.
- **Climate and aquatic vegetation:** Reconstruct local climate and relative macroalgal abundance using plant-wax distributions and compound-specific δ²H and δ¹³C measurements.
projects.contribution: My work reconstructs the climatic context and investigates how terrestrial and aquatic plant sources influence biomarker signals, including vegetation-corrected plant-wax δ²H records from Lake Rotsee.

projects.title: HOLMODRIVE · Lake Peixão
projects.summary: Reading the Lake Peixão sediment archive to understand climate, vegetation, and environmental change in western Iberia.
projects.question: How have North Atlantic climate variability, vegetation, and human activity shaped the environment around Lake Peixão?
projects.about: HOLMODRIVE investigated how North Atlantic atmospheric patterns have influenced western Iberian climate from the Late Glacial to the present. At Lake Peixão in Portugal’s Serra da Estrela, the sediment archive records changes in climate, vegetation, and the surrounding landscape.
projects.approach: Lipid biomarkers and compound-specific stable isotopes alongside pollen, sedimentology, and inorganic geochemistry.
projects.contribution:
I began by characterising the leaf-wax n-alkane distributions and isotopic signatures of dominant plants, soil, and surface sediment around the lake. This calibration identified the δ²H of the C₂₉ n-alkane as a robust indicator of terrestrial hydrology in Lake Peixão sediments and established a baseline for interpreting leaf-wax records in western Iberia.

I then applied these proxies downcore to reconstruct vegetation and hydroclimate over the last 2,000 years. The record documents shifts in Atlantic and Mediterranean climate influences through the Medieval Climate Anomaly and the Little Ice Age, linking vegetation change to large-scale atmospheric dynamics.

I also contributed to multi-proxy studies of the core’s chronology, deglaciation, and Saharan dust and sea-salt inputs since the Late Glacial.

projects.overview_text:
During my time at IPMA and the University of Lisbon, I worked on Lake Peixão, a small glacial lake at around 1,700 m in Serra da Estrela. Its position between Atlantic and Mediterranean climate influences makes its sediments a sensitive archive of environmental change in western Iberia.

I led the organic geochemistry work on the PEX19-01 sediment core, analysing leaf-wax n-alkanes and their compound-specific δ²H and δ¹³C values.
